 Common Order
The petitioners herein are Bds qualified candidates.
They possess degrees issued by the Tamil Nadu Dr.MGR Medical University.
When Medical Services Recruitment Board called for applications for the post of Food Safety Officers, the petitioners applied in response thereto.
They wrote the written examinations held on 20.10.2022.
The petitioners were called for certificate verification.

However,
the Board published a list of ineligible candidates on 13.02.2023 and the petitioners' names were included therein.
The petitioners came to know that the Board did not consider BDS degree holders as holders of Degree in medicine.

The petitioners have therefore filed these writ petitions Dr.M.Divya vs The Director (Regulations) on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178081918/
3 impugning the stand of the respondents.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 4/
2.Holders of degree in Siddha medicine filed WP(MD)No.4882 of 2023 etc., challenging the stand of the respondents holding them ineligible for the post of Food Safety Officer.
For the reasons set out in the common order dated 23.03.2023 allowing the said writ petitions, the present writ petitions also have to be allowed.
3.BDS is obviously a modern system of medicine dealing with dentistry.
It comes under the allopathic category.
The learned counsel for the petitioners would point out that for pursuing BDS course, one has to clear NEET as in the case of MBBS degree.
It is also pointed out that when the Public Service Commission of the State of Tripura issued a similar notification, it enabled BDS degree holders also to participate in the recruitment process.

entities.text: Public Service Commission of the State of Tripura
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 4.The petitioners are qualified to treat dental diseases and perform dental surgeries.
They are governed by the Dentist Act which is a Central enactment.
To exclude the petitioners who are dentists and including veterinarians who have been excluded in the definition set out in the Indian Medical Act, 1956 is irrational and perverse.
The recruiting board cannot be bound by the clarification issued by the first respondent.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 5/
No clarification can prevail over a statutory definition.
The scope and ambit of the definition has to be laid down by the court.
I, therefore, hold that BDS degree holders are also eligible to participate in the subject recruitment process.
5.The impugned list declaring the petitioners as ineligible is set aside insofar as the petitioners are concerned.
The selection list also will have to be revised as the petitioners also will have to be considered.
The writ petitions are allowed accordingly.
No costs.
Connected miscellaneous petitions are closed.
